Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations

Class BelongsTo<R extends Model>

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations.Relation<R,BelongsTo<R>>
org.aristonis.diwan.database.eloquent.relations.BelongsTo<R>
Type Parameters:
R - the related (owner) model class
public final class BelongsTo<R extends Model> extends Relation<R,BelongsTo<R>>
The inverse of a has-one or has-many relation: the model this relation is built on, the child, holds the foreign key, and it points at a column of the related owner, such as a post's author. Laravel's BelongsTo.

The lazy query is where owner.ownerKey = ? with the child's foreign key bound, read with first(). A child whose foreign key is null runs no query. Eager keys are the children's foreign keys, inlined when the owner key is the owner's integer primary key. Every child pointing at the same owner gets the same owner instance. Single use, not safe to share across threads (see Relation).

Only getResults() skips the query for a null foreign key. Relation.getQuery() and Relation.get() on such a child build and run where owner.ownerKey is null, as Laravel does; that query matches no row when the owner key is a primary key.

    • BelongsTo

      public BelongsTo(EloquentBuilder<R> query, Model child, String foreignKey, String ownerKey, String relationName)
      Creates the relation. Models normally build it through belongsTo(...).
      Parameters:
      query - an unconstrained query on the owner model, never null
      child - the model holding the foreign key, never null
      foreignKey - the child's column pointing at the owner, never null
      ownerKey - the owner's column the foreign key holds, never null
      relationName - the relation's name, used by associate and dissociate; null to take it from the model's relations() map
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if query, child, foreignKey or ownerKey is null

    • associate

      public Model associate(R model)
      Points the child at an owner: the child's foreign key takes the owner's key value and the owner is set as the loaded relation. Nothing is saved.

      The relation name is the one given to the 4-arg belongsTo or by the model's relations() map; failing that, the only map entry with this owner class, foreign key and owner key. When there is none, or more than one, only the key is set.

      Parameters:
      model - the owner, never null
      Returns:
      the child
      Throws:
      InvalidRelationException - if the name is looked up and the child's relations() map fails its check
      NullPointerException - if model is null
      IllegalStateException - if the owner has no owner key value, such as before it is saved

    • associate

      public Model associate(Object id)
      Points the child at an owner by its key: the child's foreign key takes the value and the loaded relation, if any, is unset, since the owner is not known. Nothing is saved.
      Parameters:
      id - the owner key value; null clears the foreign key
      Returns:
      the child
      Throws:
      InvalidRelationException - if the name is looked up and the child's relations() map fails its check
      IllegalArgumentException - if id is a model; pass it typed as the owner class to use associate(Model)

    • orWhere

      public final BelongsTo<R> orWhere(String column, Object value)
      Adds or column = value to the lazy query.
      Parameters:
      column - the column, never null
      value - the value
      Returns:
      this relation
      API Note:
      The relation's own constraints are not grouped, as in Laravel, so an or here widens the result past the parent's rows; group it with where(Consumer).
